subject: Service incident: root cause narrative, recovery timeline, and customer-facing action register
body:
From: Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwood.ai>
To: Rajiv Patel <rajiv@groundtruth.ai>, GroundTruth Ops <ops@groundtruth.ai>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.ai>, Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 12 May 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Service incident: root cause narrative, recovery timeline, and customer-facing action register

Hi Rajiv / GroundTruth Ops team,

Thank you again for your patience as we investigated the service disruption you experienced on 2026-05-11. Below is a concise customer-facing summary of what happened, what we did to recover, and the concrete actions we're committing to. I know compliance and procurement asked for clear timelines and evidence; this note accompanies the attachments (post-incident summary PDF + timeline CSV) and we are prepared to run a short sync if helpful.

Executive summary
- Incident window: 2026-05-11 02:57:00 UTC to 2026-05-11 04:22:00 UTC.
- Impact: intermittent token generation failures for ~8% of requests routed to the affected Dedicated shard (your traffic) with elevated latency for an additional 20 minutes during cleanup. No customer data was exfiltrated.
- Root cause (summary): a race condition in the KV cache eviction path caused overlapping eviction and restore operations on a subset of requests when autoscaling reclaimed a GPU instance. Under a specific sequence (high concurrent short-sequence inference + autoscale churn) we observed a stale cache pointer leading to a select set of requests using corrupted KV state.

Timeline (high level)
- 2026-05-11 02:57 UTC — First elevated error rate observed by internal alerting.
- 2026-05-11 03:05 UTC — On-call engineers triaged; determined errors correlated with a specific Dedicated shard group serving your region.
- 2026-05-11 03:22 UTC — Temporary mitigation: we disabled autoscale eviction on the affected pool and routed traffic to healthy nodes. Immediate error rate returned to baseline for most requests.
- 2026-05-11 03:40 UTC — Hotfix deployed (rev 3.4.11) that hard-guards KV pointers during eviction.
- 2026-05-11 04:22 UTC — Service behavior normalized; background validation sweep completed later that hour.

Technical findings (concise)
- Trigger: eviction + concurrent request path that attempted to restore KV state from an aborted eviction window.
- Failure mode: corrupted in-memory pointer used for KV cache lookups, causing invalid memory reads and per-request tokenization failures.
- Scope: limited to a small percentage of connections on the affected shard(s); we confirmed via sampling that GroundTruth AI workspace traffic saw the same signal but no persistent storage corruption.
- Data exposure: none. The corruption impacted transient in-memory state only; we verified there were no unauthorized outbound connections or persisted artifacts.

Customer-facing actions and dates
1) Immediate: we disabled eviction on the pool and deployed hotfix rev 3.4.11 (complete 2026-05-11 03:40 UTC).
2) Short-term (by 2026-05-18): additional validation added to the eviction code path and expanded test harness coverage for concurrent eviction/restore scenarios.
3) Medium-term (by 2026-06-01): a conservative autoscale policy roll-out for Dedicated pools that reduces churn under bursty short-sequence traffic and adds an extra drain step before eviction.
4) Audit & evidence (by 2026-05-20): we will provide the following artifacts for your procurement/compliance review:
   - Event timeline CSV (attached).
   - Redacted logs showing node-level events and the patch rollout (we will share a redacted slice).
   - Patch diff and test results summary (internal test harness output).

Next steps
- Please find attached: groundtruth_postincident_summary.pdf and groundtruth_timeline_utc.csv.
- If your compliance team wants the redacted logs, reply here and we will package and share via a secure transfer (S3 presigned link or your preferred SFTP).
- I propose a 30-minute sync to walk through the technical slides and answer questions. Our availability: 2026-05-13 11:00-15:00 PDT or 2026-05-14 08:00-12:00 PDT. Please let me know what works.

Apologies again for the disruption — we understand reliability is critical and are prioritizing changes to prevent recurrence.

Best,

Evelyn Hart
Sr. Customer Reliability Manager
Redwood Inference
E: evelyn.hart@redwood.ai | M: +1 415-555-0142

From: Rajiv Patel <rajiv@groundtruth.ai>

Date: Tue, 12 May 2026 11:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Service incident: root cause narrative, recovery timeline, and customer-facing action register

Thanks Evelyn — clear and appreciated. A couple of quick clarifications our security/compliance folks requested:
1) When you say "no customer data was exfiltrated," can you confirm that temporary in-memory state was never serialized or written to disk (including ephemeral logs)? We need the exact log keys/paths to show our auditors.
2) For the medium-term autoscale policy, will this be configurable per Dedicated pool (we run several)? If so, can we opt into the conservative policy now?
3) Would you be able to share the redacted node logs and the patch diff for our SRE to look at before the sync?

Also, happy to take the 30-minute sync — would prefer Wednesday morning (2026-05-13) if you have an opening around 11:30 PDT.

— Rajiv
Head of Platform Engineering
GroundTruth AI
rajiv@groundtruth.ai | +1 617-555-0099

----- Reply / message 3 -----
From: Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwood.ai>
To: Rajiv Patel <rajiv@groundtruth.ai>
Cc: Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwood.ai>, Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.ai>, Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 12 May 2026 15:20:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Service incident: root cause narrative, recovery timeline, and customer-facing action register

Hi Rajiv — quick technical clarifications below (copied from Evelyn's note for context).

On Tue, May 12, 2026 at 9:12 AM Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwood.ai> wrote:
> Executive summary
> - Incident window: 2026-05-11 02:57:00 UTC to 2026-05-11 04:22:00 UTC.
> - Impact: intermittent token generation failures for ~8% of requests routed to the affected Dedicated shard (your traffic) with elevated latency for an additional 20 minutes during cleanup. No customer data was exfiltrated.

To address Rajiv's specific questions:
1) In-memory state and logs: we verified the code paths and logging outputs. The corrupted pointer affected only the in-memory KV cache; there were no code paths that serialized that pointer to disk. Standard request logs (application-level) are written to our logging pipeline; any logs containing identifiers were redacted prior to sharing. The node-level debug traces that show eviction/restore sequence do not include plaintext customer content. We will provide a redacted log bundle (node_eviction_slice.log.gz) with clear markers for time ranges in the attached CSV.

2) Autoscale policy configurability: yes — the conservative autoscale policy will be configurable per Dedicated pool. We can opt your Dedicated pools into the conservative profile immediately; that will suspend automatic eviction for 15 minutes after a scale-down command and add an explicit drain handshake. If you want us to enable that now for one or more of your pools, tell us the pool IDs and we'll apply it today.

3) Patch diff and delivery: the hotfix (rev 3.4.11) was a focused guard around the eviction pointer lifecycle and an added assertion in the restore path. We will share the diff (redacted for internal helper functions) and the unit + concurrency test output under the Drive link. The full change will be folded into the 3.5.0 release after additional test coverage.

Logistics / evidence delivery options
- We will share redacted logs via a secure S3 presigned link (preferred) or SFTP; indicate preference.
- The timeline CSV and the summary PDF are attached to Evelyn's original email and are in the Drive folder: https://drive.redwood.example.com/teams/incident/GT-20260511/postmortem

Meeting scheduling
We have a slot Wed 2026-05-13 11:30 PDT reserved for you. If that works, Evelyn or Monica will send a calendar invite and dial-in details.

Thanks —
Dylan Brooks
Senior Site Reliability Engineer
Redwood Inference
